title: Whether knowledge is an act elicited from the habit of faith
pass_a_gloss: Article XVII. Whether knowledge is an act elicited from the habit of faith. 1. Robert Bellarmine (On Justification 1.7) says faith is not knowledge but assent, and that knowledge is a prerequisite to faith, not faith's own act. 2. Distinguishing kinds of knowledge: (1) knowledge of the terms; (2) knowledge of the proposition as proposed; (3) knowledge or judgment by which we assent. The first two are prerequisites to faith's assent; the third is either assent itself or most intimately joined to it. 3. Justifying faith is not bare historical knowledge but fiducial assent; therefore Bellarmine's distinction, if it tends to sever faith wholly from knowledge, is to be rejected. The Orthodox teach that in faith there is knowledge and assent — indeed also trust.
pass_b_english: Article XVII. Whether knowledge is an act elicited from the habit of faith.
1. Bellarmine says faith is assent, not knowledge — knowledge only a prerequisite, not faith's own act.
2. Distinguish: knowledge of terms; of the proposition as proposed; and the judgment by which we assent. The first two precede faith's assent; the third is assent itself or joined to it.
3. Justifying faith is not bare historical knowledge but fiducial assent. If Bellarmine severs faith from knowledge entirely, reject that. Orthodox: faith includes knowledge, assent, and trust.
source_text:
ART. XVII.
An notitia sit actus ab habitu fidei elicitus.

1. Robertus Bellarminus lib.1. de justificatione cap.7. dicit, fidem non esse notitiam, sed assensum; & notitiam esse praerequisitam ad fidem, non ipsum fidei actum.

2. Distinguendum est inter notitias: (1) notitia terminorum; (2) notitia propositionis ut proponitur; (3) notitia seu judicium quo assentimur. Primae duae praerequiruntur ad assensum fidei; tertia est vel ipse assensus, vel ei intimius conjuncta.

3. Fides justificans non est nuda notitia historica, sed assensus fiducialis; ideoque Bellarmini distinctio, si eo tendat ut fidem a notitia prorsus sejungat, rejicienda est. Orthodoxi docent in fide inesse notitiam & assensum, imo & fiduciam.
